messages:
Akira: FYI: noticed token-level tail increased for model-v2 on /v1/generate. 99.9% moved ~80ms -> ~230ms for a small subset. Example req=a7b2c trace=02abc3. Attaching trace + quick profiler snapshot.

Jamie: Which endpoint? internal batching or customer route?

Akira: /v1/generate (customer traffic). Affects ~0.15% of requests. Kernel selector was unchanged.

Rachel: Post the jaeger link?

Akira: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/02abc3?filter=request_id=a7b2c
Profiler snippet:
```
dispatch -> kernel_selector -> kernel_exec(matmul_fallback) -> main
matmul_fallback ~160ms for batch=1 seq=512 kv=false
```

Sven: Sounds like the selector picked a fallback kernel for that sequence length and we hit a slow codepath. Need kernel_tag/family surfaced in telemetry.

Maya: Our dashboards only show end-to-end token_latency histograms per-route today. We need a per-span/timeline breakdown (queue, select, kv_lookup, kernel_exec) so the UI can show stacked bars per-request.

Jamie: Proposal: emit low-cardinality labels with each request: kernel_family, batch_bucket (0,1,2-4,5+), kv_hit (y/n), model_variant. For sampled traces emit per-token timings and token_index (sampling rate 1/1000 default). This gives aggregates plus linkable traces.

Akira: Example Prom query for 99th token latency by route:
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
But we also need a way to jump from that panel to trace(s) — so sampled exports must include trace_id/request_id.

Rachel: Grafana idea: "Per-request breakdown" table where each row is a sampled request with columns: route, request_id, start_ts, total_ms, and a timeline column rendering stacked spans (queue | select | kv | kernel). Include a link column that opens Jaeger: jaeger://trace/02abc3?request_id=a7b2c. We'll source rows from ClickHouse that stores sampled span durations.

Sven: Cardinality warning: do NOT add request_id or token_index as Prom labels. Keep Prom labels low-cardinal: kernel_family, batch_bucket, kv_hit, model_variant. Use the sampled export (ClickHouse) for high-card fields like request_id, trace_id, token_index.

Maya: Also, token_index explodes. For metrics use token_bucket (0,1-8,9-64,65+). Keep exact token_index only in sampled logs/traces. Update sampling policy accordingly.

Akira: Sampled log example (one-line JSON we can ingest into ClickHouse):
{"ts":"2026-03-18T10:02:44Z","request_id":"a7b2c","trace_id":"02abc3","route":"/v1/generate","kernel_family":"matmul","kernel_tag":"matmul-opt-v3","batch_size":"1","batch_bucket":"1","kv_hit":"false","token_bucket":"1-8","token_index":"7","token_latency_ms":"162"}

Jamie: Action items:
1) Akira: add kernel_family + batch_bucket + kv_hit to runtime metrics (low-card) and wire a sampled per-request export to ClickHouse. (owner: Akira)
2) Rachel: prototype Grafana per-request breakdown panel (timeline + jaeger link) using sample fixtures. (owner: Rachel)
3) Sven: update sampling policy to 1/1000 default, 1/100 for slow/error requests, and ensure we have an override to always sample on regressions. (owner: Sven)
4) Maya: run a 24h targeted collection for the affected customer cohort and upload artifacts to s3://redwood-inference/perf-spike/2026-03-18/ (owner: Maya)

deploy-bot: deploy success: runtime/1.42 -> canary started on prod @ 2026-03-18T10:05Z :rocket:

Rachel: I'll build fixtures and prototype the timeline -> jaeger link this afternoon. Let's sync tomorrow 10:30 to review the dashboard and Akira's PR.

Sven: +1

Akira: Also going to add a correlation header on the API: X-Trace-Request: req=a7b2c;trace=02abc3 so SDKs can show direct trace links.

Jamie: :thumbsup:
